brief:
Palestinian citizens of Israel express alarm over the threat of far-right political gains, with concerns intensifying after recent settler provocations in villages like Majd al-Krum. Though local protests have forced some settlers to withdraw from the northern town, residents say the retreat masks deeper anxieties about what a far-right electoral victory could mean for their safety and legal standing.

The apprehensions reflect a broader pattern: as right-wing political movements gain momentum ahead of elections, Palestinians holding Israeli citizenship worry they will face escalating harassment and potential policy shifts that strip away protections. Majd al-Krum's successful resistance to settler incursions offers little reassurance, residents said, given the political climate they see taking shape.
dek: Majd al-Krum's protests have forced settlers to withdraw, but fears of further provocations loom after elections.
title: Palestinian citizens fear far-right victory will target them next
